hints: Notice the snowflake is already falling downwards when upward air resistance grows to equal downward weight, so the two arrows in the diagram cancel.
Connect balanced vertical forces to resultant force: $F_{net} = weight - air$ $resistance = 0$, and then to $F_{net} = ma$.
Ask what zero acceleration means for an object that already has a downward velocity, rather than assuming zero force means zero velocity.
walkthrough: Identify the motion: the snowflake is falling downwards on a still day, with weight acting vertically down and air resistance acting vertically up.
State the force condition: air resistance increases until its magnitude equals the weight, so the upward and downward forces balance.
Calculate resultant force: $F_{net} = weight - air$ $resistance = 0$, as stated by no resultant force acting.
Apply Newton's laws: $F_{net} = ma$, so $a = 0$. This is the terminal velocity condition where speed stops changing.
Connect to velocity: zero acceleration means velocity is unchanged, not zero. Because the snowflake was already moving down, it continues falling at a steady speed. This is option D.

options.A: Acceleration needs a resultant force with $F = ma$. Here weight and air resistance cancel, so resultant force and acceleration are zero.
options.B: Deceleration also needs a net upward force. With air resistance equal to weight there is no net upward force.
options.C: Zero resultant force does not stop a moving object. The snowflake was already falling, so it does not become stationary.
options.D: With no resultant force acceleration is zero, so the falling snowflake keeps the velocity it has reached as terminal velocity.
